text_fidelity_a:
ACDelco 2-Hour Fast Battery Charger Includes AA Rechargeable Batteries and Car Adapter, 4 Count This charger works. It comes down to preference in style, and perhaps the going price at the time you are shopping around.

Upon arrival, I immediately unpacked this ACDelco battery charger. It comes with 4 AA batteries, and since I didn't see anything on the package about them being precharged, I went ahead and plugged them into my truck adapter. I was curious how well it would do in my truck (with the included car adapter) and since I knew I was running an errand that would take no more than two hours, I figured it was a good time to try it out.

I plugged them in at 2:10 pm, and saw that the batteries were charging as indicated by the red light. When I got back into my truck (I remembered to look!), the time was 3:05, and the battery indicator light was green, telling me that the batteries were fully charged. So this 55 minute charge time (likely less, since I wasn't in the truck whole time) tells me that it charged faster than anticipated, or the batteries had a little bit of charge on them to begin with, which is more apt the case--which is nice when they can be used right out of the package. Either way, it clearly charges and works fine.

(edit to add..) I see in the lower product description that the batteries come charged. Mine weren't fully charged, but I assume half charge (or more), and my charge time just topped them off. So to test this product further, I grabbed a set of drained rechargeable batteries from another brand that I hadn't gotten around to re-charging yet. I mean, I used them but drained them. I hadn't charged them again yet because I don't care for the charger it came with, so I just keep putting it off. I LIKE THIS CHARGING UNIT, and I will explain after details..

DETAILS!
--This charger charges AA and AAA batteries. It comes with 4 AA batteries and two styles of cords 110-volt wall adapter and 12-volt car adapter

-- The cord measurement for each is as follows:
74" wall charger cord
41" car adapter cord

--Charging Time Per Battery Capacity:
AA 1400mAh - 1800mAh: 1.5 - 2 hours
AA 1800mAh - 2300mAh: 2-2.5 hours
AAA 600mAh - 750mAh: 1.5 - 2 hours
AAA 750mAh - 1000mAh: 2-2.5 hours

--So, on the face of the charger on the left hand side, there are two indicator lights: one that glows red as the batteries charge, and one that glows green when charged and ready for use. Easy peasy.

--On the right hand side, there is a switch. It is to be set to either 2 batteries, or 4 batteries (+2, +4). Among the rebels among us, I have no idea what happens if we tried charging three batteries! :O

--Within the battery placement area, the slots are numbered. 1 through 4. I wish there were more clarification on this on the product page because I can no longer find the directions it came with. I am thinking that if just two batteries are being used, and they were placed in #1, #2 slots (or #3,#4) AND the indicator switched was in place for 2 batteries, does the charging juice primarily go to those spot (so as to keep with the quick charge ability)?. I think if just two batteries are being charged, then they go in the center, in the #1 and #2 spots-- so that's my plan going forward. I imagine this information is in the little pamphlet that came with the package. I'll be back if I find it and learn anything.

--The charging batteries at no point has gotten too warm my Energizer one gets pretty warm).

MY THOUGHTS:
--I LOVE that it has the TWO charging cords, with LONG cords. First, I like that it even has a cord, period. I have the Energiizer one that is just plugged into the wall. It seems like it would take up less space, but it doesn't. I find it harder to use as I need perfect clearance to plug that thing in. With this, I just need to find an outlet, then I can have it placed further away, making it easier to see and access. With the addition of the car charger, it just adds another option. Nice for camping (flashlights, radio, etc), or if you still use non cellphone cameras that eat batteries like crazy (this is what originally got me into rechargeable batteries almost 20 years ago, the digital cameras- ugh, I'm old). I sometimes bring a speaker with me for use with smartphone. It takes AA batteries. If I think to actually carry this unit around with me, I can charge my speaker batteries on the go if need be. But I think I will use this primarily in my home. I go through batteries with use of a couple of lighted mirrors. I have one that takes 4AAA and one that takes 4AA. The lights are bright, and I tend to go through batteries- so I make sure to have rechargeables on hand. As mentioned before, I like this unit because it is easier for me to find a place to put it to plug in AND have resting nearby. I had been in need of recharging a set of batteries and just hadn't gotten around to it because I don't care for the inconvenient (to me) charging unit of the other one. It works great, but I just found I prefer to have a cord. This has a cord.

PICTURES include another brand of (depleted) rechargeable AA battery (2000mah) with start time of being placed in charging unit. Product info says AA batteries between 1800mah and 2300mah will take 2-2.5 hours to charge. I put in the batteries at 11:42 am, and at 2:18 pm they were still charging. This would be just over 2.5 hours. I got up to take my dogs outside, and when I came back an hour later, the batteries were fully charged. So, I would plan on anywhere between 2.5-3.5 for a full charge on a depleted set of batteries (from another brand). Since I have yet to fully deplete the ACDelco batteries, I can't test those out until I do.

In summation.. I find nothing wrong with it, it works mostly intended.. If I figure anything else out as I continue to use these, I will be back to update.
text_fidelity_b: ACDelco 2-Hour Fast Battery Charger Includes AA Rechargeable Batteries and Car Adapter, 4 Count

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC1200 Reliable Dual Band WiFi Router (Archer C50) Update, Aug 2016: It's been 5 months since I installed this router and it has the distinction of never needing to be rebooted yet! That's a record for me, since some of my past routers needed a reboot every week or two (or even every day or two). I continue to be impressed with the rock-solid performance of this TP-LINK. It's not fancy and lacks some high-end features, but I'll take solid, dependable performance over flash any day.

Original review:
While this router won’t satisfy the needs of those who have complex networking requirements or those who like to tinker and tweak, it offers solid performance, AC speeds and good coverage at a very reasonable price point. If you’re looking to go to AC speed but don’t want all the bells and whistles, this offers a lot for the money.

The footprint is very small compared with other routers I have, which is a nice change. The overall build quality seems very good, and the two antennae are firmly attached (another problem I’ve had with lower-end routers). It has an off switch which is handy if you need to do a reboot. It runs warm but not hot.

Setup is very straightforward if you want to keep the default settings. Basically just plug it into a PC, access the router menu with your browser, set the network name and password, and you’re done. You can access more advanced features if needed, but for a basic setup the time required is less than 5 minutes.

Performance has been impressive. I also have AC routers from D-Link and Linksys that are far more costly than this, but this little guy holds his own when it comes to coverage and throughput. For example, I get Internet connection speeds of about 62mBps with my D-Link DIR-880L. This router, with the same PC and network card, gives me 50mBps. Wireless coverage is a little more spotty with this router on fringe areas (e.g., for a PC located a floor above and at the opposite end of the house from the router) but it still maintains a connection, albeit at lower speeds.

This does lack some features that could be helpful for some situations. It has a USB port, but only has one, and it’s a 2.0 USB port. It lacks a gigabit port as well. But again, for the price, it offers a lot of performance. So far I’ve had zero problems or glitches.

This router won’t excite a power user or satisfy complex networking requirements/demands, but for the basics, it gets the job done with solid speed and performance. Well worth considering if you’re looking for an inexpensive router.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC1200 Reliable Dual Band WiFi Router (Archer C50)

text_fidelity_a:
GreatShield Ultra Anti-Glare Screen Protector Film for Kindle Paperwhite, Kindle, Kindle Touch, and Kindle Keyboard I bought this screen protector for my Kindle Touch earlier this year and love it. I just bought a Kindle Paperwhite and I had one left over from the first order. It fit perfectly, except the small gap ended up on the top and I did not realize that the line cut through the top of the menu until I turned it on to read. I'd rather have the gap at the bottom where it's not noticeable so I ordered another pack. I just got my order today and after two screens, I realized that they were too wide for the Paperwhite screen. I had to cut the last screen to get it to fit. I was bummed since it fit great before and I thought I'd get it perfect on the first try. I'm not completely happy with the final result but I don't want to pay for another pack not knowing which size I'm going to get. Also the edges used to be rounded and they aren't anymore so I can't get the edges to stick flat to the screen which makes the screen protector more noticeable, whereas on my Kindle Touch, I actually have to look carefully to see where the edges are. I just don't understand why these things changed. I don't know if I got a bad batch but if this is the size they are selling now, they shouldn't advertise that it fits the Paperwhite.
As far as applying, I give that four stars. I can normally get a bubble-free application. If anything goes wrong it's usually a speck of dust. I use compressed air and a credit card to get the best results. A credit card is more solid than the smoothing card it comes with so it works a lot better.

UPDATE 11/18/2012: The GreatShield company responded to my review and they sent me a replacement order right away. Awesome customer service from those guys. After getting my replacement, I can safely say that the order I had before was defective. The new order fit the screen perfectly and the edges are rounded. It is installed on my Kindle Paperwhite and I'm a happy customer. In light of this, I have changed my rating from 2 stars to 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: GreatShield Ultra Anti-Glare Screen Protector Film for Kindle Paperwhite, Kindle, Kindle Touch, and Kindle Keyboard

text_fidelity_a:
Pentax K1000 Manual Focus SLR Film Camera with Pentax 50mm Lens My k1000 will be 30 years old this Christmas, and it has been the most reliable camera I have ever owned. My lenses are still nice and sharp. My light meter and flash shoe still work. I have probably changed the battery 3 times. There are no light leaks. Everything works just like the day I got it.

This is a great first camera for any person who wants to learn about photography: exposure, composition, etc. With digital point and shoots, it's really easy to just be a documentarian and rely on photoshop or filters to fix things up a bit later, but there's no real incentive to get things right in the first instance. Film - real film - requires patience and discipline and a critical eye. Which is why I am teaching my 11 year old son to use this.

A tip on loading the film (I was dead broke for a lot of the first decade I owned this and could not afford to waste a bit): Before you try to load the film, bend just the last little bit down, so that it makes a little l-shaped piece that will catch in the slot. Put the tag into the slot and carefully pull out just enough to fit the film snugly into the camera. BY HAND, turn the spool on the left side about half a turn to set the film on the spool and make sure the holes are caught on the teeth. When you turn the left spool, the film should come easily out of the canister. Only do a little bit, and if it seems to be working (i.e. pulling the film out of the canister), close the back of the camera. Cock the camera - WATCH the film counter to make sure the film is advancing. If it's not, don't rewind unless you are sure you can do so without losing your leading edge into the film canister. Just open the back and re-set the edge onto the spool and try again. If it is - and you should be able to feel the resistance in the mechanism - shoot a picture. The first one won't come out. The second one may, and by loading carefully, you should be able to get an extra couple of shots on every roll of film.
text_fidelity_b: Pentax K1000 Manual Focus SLR Film Camera with Pentax 50mm Lens

text_fidelity_a:
Gypsy by Carlos Santana, Around The Neck Bluetooth Headphones with 14mm Drivers for Crisp and Clear Sound Quality, 28 HRS Playtime Bluetooth Earbuds with Remote, Built-in Mic, and Magnetic Ear Tips Our family goes through headphones like no one's business. I got these for my daughter who is kind of rough on headphones. LEt's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
BUTTONS
The buttons on this are beautifully designed. They are on the actual outside of the headphone instead of the edge. They are easy to press and locate while they are on or off.

FOLDING
These will fold up for easier storage. Be aware that they click rather loudly. At first my daughter thought she broke them and was panicked, but we realized that is a feature of the heaphones.

SOUND
The sound is pretty muffled on these headphones. It is not as clear as the Oye model from Santana.

BATTERY LIFE
They are pretty good with the life. A charge will last about six hours or so before you have to charge again. If you use them on SD card they last the six to seven hours, but blue tooth gives shorter life of around five hours.

SD CARD
My daughter loves the SD card feature. She loves to use it to listen to music. She uses the card she used to us on her phone. It is 16 GB size. When you first power on, it will go to card mode if you have the card in it. If you want to listen via blue tooth, without taking the card out, you press the power button once, and it will go to blue tooth, but it will KEEP YOUR PLACE ON THE SD card- she loves that feature.

FUNCTION BUTTONS
All of the function buttons work well. Taking calls is not as good as with other devices, but it does work and it is sufficient for making a quick call.

BASS MIDS HIGHS and VOLUME
These are very loud headphones requiring a low volume on the phone to use. (Oye requires a halfway volume on phone, Zebop only requires 1/4 volume to play at the same level of volume)

COMFORT
These are a little heavier (as comapred to Oye), AT the top of the head where the cushion is, it has silicone on it, which can catch on your hair, but it does keep them in place. The ear cups will sweat which is not uncommon with headphones.

THE BOTTOM LINE
These are well designed headphones with great features. The comfort is good, but the sound is kind of mediocre.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. Great design, nice features, these are headphones our daughter uses a lot when she is doing things that she does not want to use more expensive headphones while doing. They have good performance but not great. These are a good mid-range set of headphones and have lasted much better than other brands which were similar price range and had similar performance.
text_fidelity_b: Gypsy by Carlos Santana, Around The Neck Bluetooth Headphones with 14mm Drivers for Crisp and Clear Sound Quality, 28 HRS Playtime Bluetooth Earbuds with Remote, Built-in Mic, and Magnetic Ear Tips

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Finepix F70EXR 10MP Super CCD Digital Camera with 10x Optical Dual Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7 inch LCD This is a high quality camera, but you must take time to read through the owner's manual to understand how to get the best pictures. You can just grab it and point and shoot using it while in the "automode" setting, but the resulting pictures may leave you a little disappointed depending upon the photographic conditions. To get the highest quality photos you must become familiar with how this little beauty works. Unfortunately, you might have to print out and tote the manual with you when you find yourself in situations where your pictures aren't what you'd like, or you can't figure out how to do certain things like know what's behind the flashing icon error message, or how to simulate different types of film, or can you choose between clarity, reduced noise and dynamic range? This is not really a simple "point and shoot" camera and all images will turn out great. You will have to study it, practice with it, and most of all have patience and you will be pleasantly rewarded for your efforts. Though the indicators vary with camera settings, there are 23 different indicators just for shooting mode, and 12 for playback mode, not to mention the date/time stamp, battery level, and indicator. It can get confusing.

Although a basic manual booklet is included with the camera, a much more detailed manual must be uploaded from the enclosed CD and then all 125 pages can be printed out or read from your computer monitor. The manual covers all the material in the booklet almost page for page but includes much more information about features the booklet leaves out and the booklet will refer you to specific pages in the manual for more information. Also, in the manual are about 50 FAQ's that are very useful. I am a manual reader, (having written many technical SOP's) and appreciate having well-written and well thought out manuals that are understandable and succinct. Though I would have preferred a manual that I don't have to upload to my computer, it is well-written and many useful pictures are included.

This camera is loaded with many different options/features but accessing and understanding many of them will require reading the manual. For people who don't want to be bothered with all the bells and whistles this camera may be more than they need. I can see very serious photographers using this camera. Reading through the manual I have compiled a list of some of the various modes, options and features available:

Digital Zoom
Movie Mode
Silent Mode
Variable ISO settings
Image size selection
Aspect Ratio selection
Intelligent Face detection
Scene Position
Shooting Modes
EXR Mode
Film simulation
Dynamic Range
White Balance
Continuous Photography
Photometry - multi, spot, average

Playback Options:
Erase
Slide Show
Red-eye Removal
Image Rotation
Protection from accidental deletion
Crop
Resize
Voice Memo
Print Order
Time Difference
Format

Pages 37, 67-68, 86-87, 97-103, and 104-107 would be good to print out and keep with your camera as they contain tables of various camera functions and a trouble shooting chart.

I have taken many pictures and movies inside and out, light and dark, with this camera set on various settings. And though I have practiced with it now for several weeks, I still need to often refer to the manual when I choose to vary from automode. Some things I have found especially desirable are:

Silent Mode - I attend classical music concerts where flash photography is prohibited. This mode will silence all beeps and flashes.

Large viewing screen on the back of the camera. It is exactly 5.5cm x 4.0 cm.

Digital Zoom - extremely good. I attended a local minor-league baseball game and sat far away on the grass well beyond the playing field. I was able to fully zoom and still get good, clear, close-up shots of the players with no blurring.

Movie Mode - Completely surpasses any other I've experienced so far. Images are clear, colorful and the sound quality is excellent. Camera noise was heard and recorded while using the "zoom" function in Movie Mode though it was not very loud.

Multi-frame play back function is very useful to quickly scan for a particular picture.

Fine Pix Viewer Program was very easy to install on my computer. I use Windows XP.

Very good photography in low-light conditions.

Also some things I did not find particularly desirable but are not major flaws:

I cannot directly burn a CD using the Fine Pix Viewer Program which comes with this camera. I have to use another camera program, import the pictures into it and then burn a CD.

Very easy to accidentally turn it on or off and easy to get misfires.

The zoom lever is too sensitive. I have learned with practice to barely move it very slowly.

The camera does not give helpful suggestions on how to get a better picture as does my HP R717.

Not HD capable.

The higher the ISO the grainier the picture though a higher ISO is desirable when shooting in dim/low light levels. I have set the ISO level to 200 and that seems to produce the best pictures so far.

Almost too many options, modes and functions to choose from. Though you can immediately begin to take pictures using Automode, it will take time to fully understand the many other aspects and features this camera has.

In Summary:

I can find no major complaint concerning this camera. It takes excellent clear and colorful photos even in situations where I least expect it - indoors with no flash. Any poor quality pictures I have taken are not the fault of the camera but due to the photographer's ignorance of how to use/understand properly the many features of the camera. The basic mechanics of such things as battery and memory card installation are very easy. Battery charging is a very simple process and battery life seems long. The manual is detailed and covers more than I would probably care to know. This is almost more camera than I need, though I will continue to use it and will update this review as necessary.

UPDATE 2.9.15 - Been using this camera all these years and now it's beginning to show it's age and giving me some problems. The viewing screen on the back has a vertical big black bar but it doesn't appear on the actual pictures. And the lens cover doesn't always completely open when the camera is turned on. I still use it but it might be time to think about a replacement. It's been good though so I really don't have any complaints.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Finepix F70EXR 10MP Super CCD Digital Camera with 10x Optical Dual Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7 inch LCD

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition (32GB, White) This tablet has entirely streamlined my educational, professional, and personal productivity. I will preface this by saying I chose this tablet (as my very first tablet of any kind) after 5 WEEKS of research and hours and hours of reading the manual, watching video of reviews, unboxing, customization, how-to's, tips and tricks, and specific software guides. I had the nexus 10 in my amazon shopping cart when I first came across this tablet. I will nowhere in this review compare this to an apple device- I have never and will never own one- personal preference, I wholeheartedly believe iOS is sufficient or ideal for a lot of people's use, just not ever going to be for mine. As background, I am in an international DVM program whose laptop just crashed and all 600+gigs of my life were backed up but now only floating in cyberspace so my requirements were a little heady for a tablet-

a) deal with extensive editing and review of PDFs, PPTs, DOCs, XLXS, etc 14-17hrs a day (terms range from 21-24 credits, 4-5hrs of lecture straight, 3-4 hrs of lab with no access to outlet in many labs). Also when I say edit I don't just mean take notes on I also mean incorporate text, figures, etc from textbooks, websites, and other documents.

b) Be a textbook reader and rarely a e-book reader (novels for fun!) Need to access my extensive kindle library, plus some google books and a few Elsevier/pageburst textbooks. Also this needs to be something I am comfortable and accepting of to literally study off of, enough to give up my previous preferring to only study off of paper/actual printed out notes

c) Allow for flawless email, web chat, skype video and text, some web browsing, and file transfer... all on an absolutely horrible school wireless and LAN setup, unpredictable power availability, etc.

d) Streaming and downloading of podcasts, video, MRI, CT, radiographs, and ECG's

e) Be portable to the clinic and the farms for patient-side transcription, recording, etc

f) Get me through the 5-6hr flight and all the airport time!

g) Occasionally watch videos/listen to things for fun

h) Most importantly, due to a dominant hand injury, multiple surgeries, and continued required hand therapy/rehab, I am currently able to write again but not to type with that hand. I therefore wanted a tablet that was stylus intensive- not just for notes, but for navigation, etc. THIS is what made me give up that wonderful squeaky clean android OS of the nexus 10! (I still thing that is probably the best thing for people that want an android tablet but don't NEED a stylus)
So my tablet arrived flawless and flawlessly. The display is beautiful, if anything the screen is too bright- I'm aware my eyes are light sensitive so this won't match with the majority of people but if I do turn my brightness on at all I don't believe I've ever gone above 15%, though I'm sure there will be some case videos poorly and darkly shot that I may need to in the future.

i) at least temporarily, replace my laptop and download and have as much of my backed up laptop files as possible

The tablet was quickly populated with the apps from my HTC phone and google account. The account set up for everything was quick and easy. The initial 2 updates were completed with no adverse signs. Navigation was great, no lag, and I quickly cleared out the stock widgets, set up my panes, and then went into settings.... I activated Developer options and did some customization and disabling there, but most of the disabling I did in app manager, device, and controls. There are very helpful guides out there if you're not sure which apps are safe to disable as well as a "Guide: Longer Battery Life- How You're Being Robbed on XDA that takes you step by step in maximizing your tablet. It was not created at the time when I cleaned up mine but it would've helped greatly!

Here is the gist. The tablet comes crammed full of software and capabilities that I don't need or want. The My Magazine app, a lot of the touchwiz stuff, the eye movement sensors(smart screen), the hand gesture stuff, reading mode, voice control, motions/palm motions, all of that is just a constant battery drain and I will never use them. They were disabled and the vibration feedback for everything was also turned off.

Battery Report: This tablet was shipped within the US twice, and was brought internationally on a plan 4 days later. It was accidently left on the ENTIRE time for about 8 days with six apps up on standby. It arrived with 18% battery left. I use it for 15-17hours a day and end up having to charge it 2-3hrs per about ever 24hr period to get it back to 100. I can use it while it is charging and it will still positively charge during use.

USE FOR A STUDENT: It has replaced textbooks, laptop, printer, scanner, and painstakenly editing and customizing notes and making documents for me. Disclaimer: as someone who used to be able to type 130+ words per minute, I'll make perfectly clear, if you prefer to type and plan on typing a LOT tablet touchscreen keyboards SUCK. This is a fact of life. You can get used to them, you can get proficient at them, but you'll still probably hate it and you're going to need a physical keyboard case/add on if you do a lot of typing of documents or emails. Now, this tablet is made for a stylus. This is not just a peculiarly edged simple piece of plastic that you can buy for just about any touchscreen device and kind of use as a writing device. This is the s-pen, a WACOM and this device and stylus is designed to maximize the experience so you are writing or drawing digitally with an experience just like on paper. Examples- the harder you press the more solid and thicker your pencil/pen/brush/highlighter/calligraphy/etc line. The button on the stylus brings up air command which can be super helpful and it also allows quick screen shots. The stylus allows for fine website navigation that allows you to open drop down windows etc as mouse would. It also offers things a real pen/pencil cant- selective erasing, and selection for drag/drop/copy/paste of ANYTHING to ANYWHERE. You're typing notes and see a great figure and text on a website, you can freehand or rectangular circle what you want and put it into your document. Then you can resize/edit. It's great. I've been using the Snote app for everything thus far, I have made short futile attempts with Lecture Notes and Evernote but I couldn't really get anywhere. I'm not going to give up on then, I just need to research them more to see if I can eventually get them to do what I want and then I can compare them to Snote.

USE FOR A PROFESSIONAL: So far, this has been wonderful. I can seamlessly take notes, look up references, voice record my exam findings, and awkwardly as only a tablet is, take video and pictures of patient's during an exam for later review. (Extremely helpful during lameness and neuro exams for the file). Collaborative documents through Polaris office and google drive is exceptional- as fast as a laptop and more portable, and better screen size than a smartphone. It runs better than the school computers for running presentations off of onto projectors. I can also have students I tutor digitally sign- literally our weekly sheets and submit them via email with one step- completely negating the awesome printer and scanner I brought down here.

USE FOR A CONSUMER: I find this tablet beautiful for watching movies and videos and the sound is great. In a classroom of 50 people chatting between classes I have no problem hearing the speakers among the hub but there are completely valid reports that even cranked the sound might get lost a little if you're in a very loud close crowd. Sound improves with earbuds but the initial audio set up app (basically a hearing test and then a customized audio scheme for you) was startling when it compared the stock/base line settings to what it came up with for ME.

USE FOR AN ARTIST: I'm still learning and adapting, I'll never turn to this instead of actual physical art supplies and paper but it is fun and I can really see myself doing more digital than before. It has been especially nice for graphic design, photoshopping, etc.

USE AS A LEFTY: no issues except see below for one thing that affects both right and left handers...

ISSUES: 1) One day after about a week of ownership, my battery was in the upper 80's, I was taking some notes and about 2hrs later I looked at the status bar and it was 29%. I went into Battery in Settings, and the s-pen interface was responsible for 80% of the battery use. I shut down and then restarted and it's never happened again. Similarly the Android OS did the same thing at a later instance but again it was a one time thing and in both cases the battery recharged speedily after and stayed charged.
2) Snote- I have had weird episodes where an import fails, or it force closes itself repeatedly when I try to rename or change the cover of one particular document. After this erratic behavior occurred twice in three days and completely clearing and restarting Snote from scratch (everything backed up and replaced on my Samsung account) to no avail, I did a factory reset. The last ¾ of my ownership have seen no such problems any more. I will warn you that if you wipe out S note and you start from scratch in it and re-transfer all your SNote files back in, if you have a lot of really big files, it can take a really long time to re-populate.
3) The menu/return and physical home button- occasionally based on the desk I'm at, if my arm isn't supported and my wrist is resting fully on the edge of the tablet, these buttons will get pressed while I'm writing. Its purely an annoyance and doesn't affect the writing or do anything but I definitely have to reposition if I find I'm getting lazy on holding my wrist up at these desks.

Wrap up: I only use in landscape, it's just like writing on a portrait piece of paper except you can also zoom. I got used to writing on the tablet and the tiny stylus very quickly but there are compatible Samsung styli of various widths and sizes out there as well. I thought about waiting for the new 12.2 whose screen is literally a full piece of paper landscape, but I realized this is perfect for me and more portable than the 12.2 will be (this thing can just squeeze into one of the pockets on one of my lab coats. I was planning on having to use the Nova launcher to avoid any lag but truly, this tablet was a speed demon already and I eventually got Nova solely for the customization ability and cleaner interface. It allows me to avoid more things I don't use and I didn't lose ANY of the software I do.

Bottom line, RESEARCH! PREPARE! And there will STILL BE A LEARNING CURVE! But it will be based on discovering unexpected cool features instead of on frustration). If you won't heavily use the stylus, don't spend the money on this tablet. If you're just curious if you could "get into a stylus" try one out first but prepare first so you can use it to the full advantage while you're there. Also, I came from NO tablet and no Samsung/Note experience and there are changes between the previous model and this. You don't actually lose much but things are moved around and different. Don't be scared to optimize it, I'm not talking rooting, though adventurous forays into that terrain have finally arrived as well. In conclusion I love it, it has made things so much more efficient for me, I get a lot DONE with it and it's basically all I have to carry around. I purchased the 32gig tablet plus a 64gig Sandisk XC which installed and worked like a charm. There are annoyances that come up but any issue I have had I have been able to fix. I have everything safely backed up on Carbonite and there's a million ways to sync all of your accounts if you chose (note some of this may be unnecessary or frequency can be dialed back too)

It performs and looks beautiful and I am still learning.

EDIT: FLASH PLAYER: This tablet absolutely supports flash. Youtube and embedded flash worked right out of the box, however, to watch my amazon video's etc, I just downloaded the following file- I cannot post the actual link but it's a drop box file. Install this and make sure flash is enabled in your browser settings/plugins and it will work in the stock browser, Dolphin, and Mozilla. Some people also recommend having your browser set to View Desktop site.

Edit 12/15/2014: Please see my comment under product question- "Can you use amazon prime video on the galaxy 10.1 2014 ed? asked by Judith C. Love on November 14, 2013" for instructions and the direct link for flash file

Edit 02/2017: My tablet got slammed by careless sleep-deprived brain addled 4th year vet students and the screen got shattered in the upper right corner. Still useable, not any real issues but concern about the little chips and cracks gradually loosening and only being held together by the screen protector I was itching to replace due to scratches but now couldnt, left me with the desire to replace as I was 4 months out of my extended warranty. Call it coincidence but literally as I powered up the replacement, this original tablet FAILED. The screen doesn't illuminate. At certain angle/light you can see it's on but there is no way for me to see well enough to unlock the screen and at least access over 3 years of my life on the original tablet. I am 99% convinced this is secondary to the trauma/screen break, and I had nearly everything backed up via Carbonite on the original except for the past few months of random downloads. Still, I am grieved and wanted a moment of silence.

Yes we had great times together but I am truly sad and a bit devastated because the replacement came with OS updates that I had been actively refusing to install for the past year. Thus, my new tablet in short, I can't stand. It's the same make and model except offers 4G which I don't use but it is unbearably slow (cant load my pdf vet school notes worth a damn- it's faster for me to find a computer, login to carbonite back up, download the enormous file and open it on the computer than to scroll through the pdf on the tablet one page per 10 seconds loading. It's truly unbearable. All the updates and changes are awful and its so slow despite me instantly ditching touchwhiz and using Nova Launcher.

Moment of silence for my beloved original, maybe one day science will advance enough for me to communicate with you without a working screen so that I can have you back. Laughingly, the one OS update I did do that slowed you down, turns out, compared to the ones that followed, you were still almost the speed of light comparatively.

Kinivo customer support was very responsive, got back to me quickly with detailed instructions on various things to try. I did make some changes to settings and learned quite a bit about the product.

It turned out right clicking on the Bluetooth Device icon on the lower right on my computer screen (mine is in "hidden icons”) and selecting "Receive a File" was the final step needed. Now no problem transferring photos from my phone to my computer.

I was very impressed with how quickly customer support got back to me when I sent my first email. Took several emails but Brian was courteous and obviously wanted a satisfied customer. All that support comes with a product that only cost $9 with free shipping. Very happy with my purchase.

The first thing I noticed when I turned on the unit was that it talked to me and charted out the steps to pair the speaker to the iPhone 5. The second thing I noticed was the sound. Don't be a bonehead! It flabberghasts me that anyone would criticize this speaker. If you actually listen to the sound quality of singers and instruments, or enjoy deep full sounds, spend the money (im on the cheap side) and get the Big Jambox. And dats da facts Jack.

Streaming video doesn't seem to cause any problems with any of the input devices or either TV. The normal solution is to cycle the power off and back on. Either way, I'm looking for a better product, and most of the ones in this price range seem to be identical except for the name on the box. text_fidelity_a:
Incipio Highland Folio Case for Fire Phone, Black I had noticed that a huge percentage of people in the Middle East have folio cases for their phones, but I've seen so few here in the States that this was a big surprise to me. I like the idea a lot if you're keeping this in a purse or a pocket with a bunch of other stuff, but I've long ago reserved an entire pocket for my phone. In the case of a pocket, all this added texture actually makes it harder to get the phone out. And I can see the drawback others' mention about it not keeping itself shut; this could be a problem in the case of a purse with keys and all kinds of junk rolling around in there.

I really like the materials, however, to include the thin metal backing and the faux leather front. It stands up fine for a phone, but when you're already adding this amount of thickness, it seems like you could build some stopping points into the inside front cover. Of course that would mess up the credit card pocket. And speaking of that pocket, it seems like a good idea, if you can refrain from cramming so much into it that your phone becomes your wallet. I have another pocket on most pants, which I reserve for my wallet and keys; makes me wonder how other people live in such disorganization.

It's a pretty good quality product, and I suspect if you're looking for a folio case, you won't find one better. However, the point of the cover not staying shut is valid and maybe a reason to continue your research.
text_fidelity_b: Incipio Highland Folio Case for Fire Phone, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) This is a good tablet for the price, but it is really crippled by the lack of support for the Google Play store. I have purchased many apps for my Android smartphone that I cannot run on this tablet because they are not available in the Amazon store. Others are available on Amazon, but I would have to pay for them again to run them on this tablet (I could download them without additional cost on other Android tablets that support the Google Play store). Support for the Amazon Prime cloud services is great, though not much different from what you would get on other Android tablets.

If you mostly run free apps, then this tablet is worth considering. If you would have to re-buy a lot of apps that you have already purchased for other Android devices, then this tablet may not make financial sense for you. Other Android tablets cost more, but can give you a much brighter and sharper screen and faster performance.

Yes, some people are hacking the Amazon Fire tablet to add Google Play support, but the process is somewhat time consuming and complicated. If you're smart enough to do that, in the time it takes you to perform this hack, you could easily earn enough money to buy a better tablet in the first place.

Pen in the photo for size reference, along with the box it came in.

Unboxing was “frustration free” as advertised. I recycled my Logitech cord that connected to my desktop and inserted the USB receiver in it and it worked.

I plugged in the Micro USB charging cable to the keyboard and mouse. Only one Micro USB charging cable came with the combo so I used an extra Android Micro USB charging cable to charge both at the same time.

I was able to use the keyboard and mouse in a few moments. My computer automatically updated the files needed in a few minutes.

All in all the unboxing and set up was quick and effortless. Now I am going to explore the keyboard.

This keyboard has no number side keyboard that makes it smaller.

It has a blue function key to access page up, page down, home, and end, on the lower right where the left, right, up, down keys are.

Along the top with the F keys are blue function commands:

Escape has “Media” – when pressed opened Wave Pad, a NCH program I have installed.

F1 has an >/||, which did nothing when pressed

F2 has |<<, which did nothing when pressed

F3 has >>|, which did nothing when pressed

F4 has a speaker symbol )x, That mutes sound

F5 has a speaker symbol - which lowers volume

F6 has a speaker symbol + which increases volume

F7 has a symbol for home, which opens a new browser tab

F8 has a symbol of a magnifying glass that opens a search side window and uses Bing for search, when I clicked on one of the search results it opened a new Chrome tab. I had Chrome already opened.

F9 has a symbol for a folder, which did nothing when pressed

F10 has a symbol for power which turned off my computer. Since I had programs opened my computer asked for permission so I canceled.

F11 has “insert” on it which is pretty self explanatory

F 12 has “PrtSc” for print screen

The action on the keyboard is nice and a lot quieter than the Logitech keyboard I am replacing. The mouse action is good and also quiet.

For less than $23 this is a good keyboard and mouse. I never used the number keys on the side of my Logitech keyboard, which needed batteries, as did the mouse that came with it. The mouse had begun to do double clicks when I clicked once and the keyboard “enter” would stay down. That's why I replaced them for this Arteck Keyboard and Mouse combo. To be able to stop buying and replacing batteries and the small space it takes up, along with it is quiet, makes my money well spent.
text_fidelity_b: Arteck 2.4G Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo Ultra Compact Slim Stainless Full Size Keyboard and Ergonomic Mouse for Computer/Desktop/PC/Laptop and Windows 10/8/7 Build in Rechargeable Battery

After working with glitchy, draggy old computers for the last year or so, this is a huge revelation for me. Not only is it fast on a task-to-task basis, but the startup and shutdown processes are incredibly fast. It's not wasting my time. Nor does it waste my time with a lot of bloatware. One thing I was skeptical about was the placement of the power button on the side. I was sure I'd be turning the laptop on or off accidentally, but I've discovered that it's not that simple, which is a load off my mind.

I could wish for a couple more USB ports particularly as I use both a wireless mouse and because there's no disk drive, so I have to attach an external one when I want to access files on disk. Eh, I'll survive it. There are always work-arounds.

Bottom line is that this laptop is a perfect match for me. I'm a writer (not a gamer) and this runs all the software I need, runs it fast and efficiently, and has tremendous storage capacity for all my files. I really couldn't have asked for more. Nicely done, HP.

I only take it off to charge and to shower. Just a good fit and feel. I can customize how snug or loose I want it with ease. Very happy!

Two reasons that led me to ordering new Fitbit Sense bands:
1. I usually use the silicone bands, but the last set I bought weren't quite long enough leaving me fearful that I would lose my pricy smart watch. So I wanted a band that felt secure.
2. My last set of bands didn't have holes that made for a perfect fit. Always seemed like it was too loose feeling or too tight. It was irritating. I hoped to find a new band that offered a better fit.

As one with sensory issues, having a good fit is important. I don't care for elastic style bands (they stretch out, feel sloppy), but I began sniffing around them thinking that it would at least feel more comfortable over what I had been using. But then I stumbled upon these "Bcuckood Nylon Loop" wristbands. I saw that they arent stretchy (yay!) but that they do have a velcro closure. I was intrigued! I figured that would give me the option for a custom fit, that I can loosen or tighten with ease.. so I went ahead and ordered them.

Also chose them because they say they fit wrist sizes 6.3" to 8.7". My wrists are exactly 7", but all the wrist bands that only mention it fitting up into the 6-7.5" wrists aren't long enough when you consider that the band needs to overlap in order to be securely on (as well as fit over width of hand & thumb). I figured this was a winner when I saw 8.7"

These are GREAT. Very happy. Love the colors. Easy on, and for the most part, easy off. I have wide pals, so sliding this off means that I am really loosing it up to do so, but I have gotten used to it and it isnt weird.

The velcro are neat. They are in little disks. Really grabs the material securely. I really like how secure this band feels. I love the best off all how I dont feel like I am wearing a watch. This band makes my wrist feel free.

So far, no stink. But Ive only been wearing it a couple of weeks during the winter. So not much sweat to consider, and frankly I havent been engaging in sweaty exercise.

You get to choose what to see on your screen when you press the button, I went with steps, goal, distance and time. You can also add the date, calories and heart rate if you are wearing a strap.

I absolutely love how it feels, it doesn't bother me at all, you don't have to wear it real tight and the silicon is very soft.

The reason I took one star off is that the beep sound which comes on after one hour of inactivity (when the red warning line appears) is way, way, way too quiet. text_fidelity_a:
Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google I ordered the 'Geeni, Sentry Floodlight Security Camera with Motion Sensor, Intruder Alarm and Audio Video Recording' for review and would like to share my thoughts.

So I have had this camera for a while now and finally got it installed a couple of weeks ago and I am ready to share my thoughts and experience so far. This camera requires hard wiring which is why it took so long to get it installed. In my old home it was going to require me to get an extension cord, drill through my wall in the garage and plug it in, in the garage. This was much more work than I had anticipated. Now the new home already had normal motion sensor lights installed on switches, which made this more feasible for me to install. I took one of the motion sensor lights down and had to retrofit a new mount out of a piece of wood to cover the original hole left by removing the old light. This wasn't to hard to do and the Geeni light mounted with ease. Once installed and I turned the light switch on, it was ready to set up which took some time to do. I had to reset the device several times to get the App to set it up properly which was a quite pain however.

The camera itself is very good but so far I am not happy with all the notifications that I get which seem to be false alerts. It seems that everything seems to trigger this thing with absolutely no control as to how sensitive you would like the sensor to be. This is truly my main con with this device. I ended up turning notifications off on my mobile device which kind of defeats the purpose really.

Then there is the App which has thus far been pretty buggy. It has crashed many times and it is not so easy to find the "actual" activity that it seems to detect. Of all the motion activity that it detects, I would say that only 40% of it is relative. I do have the App set to just record everything (continuous) on the 128gb SD card which makes more sense seeing as there are so many false readings.

As for the good of this Geeni device, the image quality both during daytime and nighttime recording and playback is great. There is very little lag when accessing the footage which is surprising as I have other WiFi cameras that are painfully slow to connect and playback footage. This is probably my favorite feature (when the App doesn't crash).

Overall I do like this motion sensor and think that there is absolute value to it. I am however, really hoping for a firmware update which might help with some of the issues and allow you to adjust the sensitivity of the motion detection. Also it would be nice to have an easier way to track down and view "actual" activity rather than having to try and find that exact moment of capture. It seems to just tag a portion of footage, and you need to watch several minutes before you can find what it detected. You are also able to save the footage via the App, but doing so can take several days for it to show up on your mobile device which is another downside to this device.

I hope that this was helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google

It doesn’t block out 100%, but I’d say it knocks out about 85% of room noise. It’s really appreciated in a houseful of rowdy kids and several multimedia devices running at the same time. Pass through sound works with a quick double tap. Thirdly, they fit well. They don’t fall out and are comfortable to my ears for the duration of the battery life. They include three sizes of inserts, so fitting was easy.

There is one thing I really dislike. Micro usb. It’s the reason I deducted a star from my rating. Why, oh why, does this device use micro usb for charging? Why force me to clutter up the floor with another cable? Stupid decision to forgo usb c for micro usb.

I can’t really speak for phone use or the Alexa functionality because I don’t use it. I disabled the microphones in the software. Don’t want amazon or anyone else intruding into my private life.

Over all, these are great buds; I use them everyday.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Buds (1st Gen) – Wireless earbuds with immersive sound, active noise reduction, and Alexa

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung 840 EVO 250GB 2.5-Inch SATA III Internal SSD (MZ-7TE250BW) The drive delivers on the SSD promise: very fast access times, even on an older computer supporting SATA1 only. The computer boots up so fast it reminds me of old days before operating systems became so bloated. (Yes, I'm talking pre-history.)

However, as others have noted, the software supplied with it for migration is just terrible, it only works if everything is perfect. And the instructions and error messages are completely inadequate (mostly missing, really).

I wanted to do more than complain, however. I figured I'd share some experience and some tips, that might help another user.

My existing disk was a 1TB hard drive that had some bad sectors (hence my desire to replace). I removed enough data from it to reduce the usage down to about 160GB, figuring that was good for a 250MB destination disk. Then I tried the Samsung cloning software. Many times. It kept failing, sometimes early, often after a few hours. With no useful information (unless you count obscure error codes that are not documented to be information). I tried running disk defrag, achieved no useful result, other than a failure after the cloning reported 100% complete. Deeply frustrating.

I couldn't do a system image restore, because Windows (Microsoft is another producer of dumb and unfriendly software) will only do a restore to a disk of the same configuration. (Here the message is simply that it "can't find a suitable disk", you have to hunt to figure out why.) And I wasn't about to buy a 1TB flash drive.

And I wanted to give it one good try before settling for reinstalling from scratch, because I didn't want to spend several more days getting my computer back to where it was.

Solution: I highly recommend using defraggler (from Piriform) to clean up your disk. You might also find it useful to shrink your partition to the minimum possible, using the WIndows disk management tool. Then I highly recommend using the Macrium Reflect Free Edition to do an "intelligent" clone of your OS volume to the SSD.

After I did this, everything worked perfectly, no problems. Wish I'd known about these tools and all the gotchas ahead of time.

Another tip: If you want to set AHCI in the BIOS (yes, now I'm getting to advanced users), you may need to first enable the AHCI drivers, otherwise Windows will not boot up (you'll get a BSOD). Do a search for this, there's a Microsoft KB article.

Good luck!
text_fidelity_b: Samsung 840 EVO 250GB 2.5-Inch SATA III Internal SSD (MZ-7TE250BW)

Acer G236HL Bbd 23-Inch Screen LED-Lit Monitor I would love to give a higher rating, but I think "1 star" is the only way to summarize my experience with this product.

Amazon shipped quickly (as usual). I tried to put it together the night it arrived. It comes in 3 pieces: base, arm, and monitor. The only instructions were a simple diagram showing how they roughly fit together. The base and arm fit together nicely, but the arm would not snap into the monitor. I could see how it was designed to snap together, but the metal part was too large to fit into the space on the back of the monitor. I could technically place the monitor on top of the arm+base, but it was very loose and could easily fall over if bumped slightly.

I called Acer tech support, hoping there was some trick I couldn't figure out. There wasn't. After suggesting that I push harder (I had already pushed hard enough that I was worried about breaking the monitor), go back to the store for assistance (huh?), and return the entire monitor, they agreed to send a replacement part.

1.5 weeks later, I called back asking for a status update on the part. I was informed that the part hadn't been ordered (huh?) and that I could call back the next day to have it ordered (wtf?). The rep agreed that this was a less-than-wonderful customer experience, but explained that there was nothing she could do (she wasn't allowed to place the replacement part order).

At that point, I gave up and started the return process with Amazon (which, btw, is always awesome when I have to do it).

So, I guess this is mainly a review of Acer QA and customer service, both of which completely failed for me. Considering the other reviews, I'm hoping that my experience is rare, but I'll be trying a different brand for my next monitor.

Pros.
1. The plastic screen finally looks good. There was always a gap between the screen and the I Phone glass. That gave it a cheap look. That gap is gone. The plastic screen goes flush against the I phone glass and looks much better.
2. We have never dropped our phones, but this case gives us a great feeling of security. At $ 800 or so per phone, it's really cheap insurance.

Cons.

Place the phone inside, after cleaning both screens. Click the plastic pieces together, then place the rubber on. Keep massaging the rubber until it fully envelopes the plastic tightly. text_fidelity_a:
Creative Sound Blaster Roar 2 Portable NFC Bluetooth Speaker with aptX/AAC (Black) I am an audiophile but I always take into account the nature of the product that I am looking at or listening to. One cannot possibly expect a $99 portable bluetooth speaker to have legitimate audiophile sound. In this case, we're talking about the Creative Sound Blaster Roar. And that assertion is not in any way a knock on this product. I bought one a few days ago and I like it and am quite happy with the purchase for a variety of reasons. The main reason I like it is because the sound it produces is GOOD. That sound is not great nor is it bad. Perhaps the worst credible thing you might say about the sound is simply that it is FINE. When I consider the size of the unit (and the size of the very small speakers it contains) and the cost, I judge the sound to be GOOD. You are not going to get Martin Logan or Definitive Technology sound out of the Roar, plain and simple. Nor will you get super sound out of any of the other competitive products such as the Bose or JBL, etc. I think they all produce generally good sound for the money. The best and smartest thing a buyer can do is perhaps go to
Best Buy or any of the other retailers who carry such units and give them all a listen and look at the features they offer and then buy the one that meets your needs in terms of both sound quality and features. Having said that, for me the Roar has more features than any of the
competing units. That is simply fact and not opinion. Most of the products that are in this category seem to be made well but in my opinion, the Roar seems to be made just a little sturdier. I haven't tested that notion by dropping my Roar on the floor but in my hands it simply feels
more robust. Back to the sound question.....since I seriously doubt that many users of portable bluetooth speakers plan on doing serious
listening that entails sitting in a quite room and doing nothing but listening intently to these little portable speakers, consider how they will actually be used. Most people are playing them as background music while they are doing other things such as sitting on the beach or
cooking on the grill or in the kitchen, etc. Critical listening ain't happening here. So let's not talk about sound imaging or speaker spatiality etc. That said, for me, I don't like speakers that have a bass response that overwhelms everything else. I want a more natural sound, One that is

more balanced to my ear. Because of that, I will gravitate towards something like the Roar. If you are one who wants more bass, then you will assuredly better like the sound of any Bose product as they have made a fortune producing bass heavy products for the last 50 years. Again, for me, the features are a big deal and the Roar excels inn that regard. I won't waste your time talking about them as you can look such things up just as easily. And price is a big deal to me. The Roar 1 can be had for $99 now.... so I bought one. The Bose is $299 the last time I checked,...three times the cost of the Roar. So simply put, I loved the price of the Roar, the feature list is unmatched, it feels like military grade construction and lastly, I thought the sound was GOOD. That's why I bought it.
text_fidelity_b: Creative Sound Blaster Roar 2 Portable NFC Bluetooth Speaker with aptX/AAC (Black)

Assembly is very simple and needs no additional tools to set it together. It also fits well into my ears. I have been using this set for the last three weeks and it works great. It is paired with my cell phone and I use this to listen to the incoming calls and also listen to the music from micro SD card inserted into the cell phone. It is small and has a discreet design. It is very light, easy to carry and works great. The gadget also synchronizes easily with phone, but it does not pair with my Garmin Nuvi GPS machine or my Acer Chromebook both of which are Bluetooth-enabled.

Pairing with cell phone is very easy; just turn the headset on and the cell phone on, it detects the Bluetooth easily and within a minute it gives the message that it is paired. The built-in battery is excellent, and on one charge it lasts for about 5-6 hours of use time. The downside is that this piece doesn't have a separate mute button or the volume button; you have to control volume from your cell phone. Another negative feature is that the three replacement parts for earpiece that comes with the set are of same size, hence gives little option for someone with small (or large) ears. I have rated this product four stars for overall satisfaction.

text_fidelity_a:
Creative Technology Speaker - Wireless - Bluetooth - USB, Bluetooth This is the second "Creative" brand wireless bluetooth speaker with microphone, and so far, the sound quality has not been very good. The first, "Creative Sound BlasterAxx SBX10 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Microphone" was $127.04 (list price $149.99), and this one currently has a list price of $199.99. I cannot hear any discernable difference in sound quality, though this speaker is larger than the other. They are both OK for being usb powered, but there are better-sounding products out there for the same price if you are willing to sacrifice the speaker option.

I ran the same tests on this speaker as the other and got identical results:

This one gets a mixed review for the overall sound quality, but it does have some features that make it very useful. I will be reviewing its various features individually so you can better assess if this meets your needs or not. I used a decibel measuring app on my phone to determine when the speakers began to distort some of what I played.

Playing audio with Bluetooth or via USB with a computer:
-There is no noticeable difference with playback using Bluetooth versus USB connection to a computer, and it has a Very long range (I walked about 25ft away and it was still doing fine)

AUDIO

75 DECIBELS AND UNDER:
Almost all audio was fine: clear, undistorted, and with pretty good clarity (don't expect GREAT quality or clarity. Just Good.) Some types of music fared poorly even at this relatively soft volume. I used "Fortuna from Carmina Burana" to test the system's limits. (YouTube the piece if you want to know which song I refer to--you'll recognize it immediately) The chorus of singers sounded distorted. At higher volumes, even as lot as 85db, it was awful. Other types of music were fine (orchestra music, pop, hip hop, electronica), but sometimes the treble was a bit fuzzy.

75-85 DECIBELS:
This is the maximum volume the speakers can reach with the USB connection, so it can get loud enough for a small-medium party, but not Very loud.
It's hit and miss here. The treble and bass have some problems, especially treble. The clarity diminishes and any nuances in your music will generally get a bit lost or muffled. Choral music, music with higher pitched percussive elements, and some types of rock and orchestra music don't sound very good.

PHONE CALLS:
The voice of the person you are calling sounds a bit muffled--definitely not as good as headphones or the phone, but about on par with other Bluetooth systems I've tried.

The voice of the speaker (i.e. You) is actually clear! This part gets a solid review. With my built-in car Bluetooth system, as well as detachable ones I've reviewed, usually the person you are calling has trouble hearing you and can experience interference. Maybe that is because it is in the car and there's road noise, but in any case, the fact this one does, actually, sound clear to the recipient of your phone call is a BIG plus.

Overall, this is a good product when you compare it to other desktop laptop speakers. If you are comparing it to products specifically meant for enjoying audio, however, I would recommend the Pioneer Electronics Audition Series for a relatively inexpensive but high quality experience, or Bose if you are looking for something higher-end. The price of the Pioneer product is almost the same, and while it doesn't have Bluetooth unless you buy the attachment separately (about $70) and it only docks with the older iPhone and iPods, the sound quality of that one is stunning. If you want extra features like FREE Bluetooth and speakerphone capability, this one is ok for the price. Not great. Just ok.

Because this is basically the same as the "Creative Sound BlasterAxx SBX10 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Microphone", and the other is about $70 cheaper, I would recommend getting the SBX10 and saving your money. They are basically the same thing, so either pay more and get better sound quality with another product entirely, or pay less for the same thing.
text_fidelity_b: Creative Technology Speaker - Wireless - Bluetooth - USB, Bluetooth

text_fidelity_a:
Netgear R7500-200NAS Nighthawk X4 Ultimate Gaming Router - AC2350 4X4 MU-MIMO Dual Band WiFi Gigabit Router (R7500v2) with Open Source Support. Compatible with Amazon Echo/Alexa I'm not a gamer, but I do have around 30 devices connected to a home network. These include WEMO switches, Amazon Echos, a smart TV, a playstation, Kindles, iPads, printers, and smartphones. The "dynamic Quality of Service" feature of this NIGHTHAWK X4 ULTIMATE GAMING ROUTER (R7500v2) seems to prioritize these devices, so that all of them are more responsive (faster connections) than they were with my previous router (a rock-solid NIGHTHAWK (R7000)).

When this NIGHTHAWK (R7500v2) is set up, it recognizes all of the "Internet of things" devices for what they are. In the "attached devices" list, these aren't given device names (e.g., "iPad", picked up from the device itself) but have "n/a" in the name column (and you can't assign them names even if you know them by the MAC numbers). I don't know exactly how the "Quality of Service" feature performs its magic, but now when I ask an Amazon Echo to turn on a light or a fan, the Echo performs the task immediately--instead of with a delay while it searched through the router's list of connected devices for the correct one.

The PCs and other devices that use lots of bandwidth (instead of being on standby much of the time) seem to connect faster, and they test (using OOKLA) at significantly faster Internet speeds.

My R7500v2 is broadcasting signals for both bands (2.4 GHz and 5 GHz), and my compatible devices connect with the 5 GHz network whenever I ask them to. However, I don't use the 5 GHz band for anything at present (because it's easiest to have everything that uses a printer on the same band with the printers). Thus I don't know whether the router frequently drops the 5 GHz signal, as other reviewers have stated.

I've used several high-end Linksys routers, and they have performed very well. However, I find that Netgear routers lose their Internet signal far less often, and almost never require rebooting--when Netgear routers need rebooting, the issue is almost always traceable to Comcast problems.

Another reason that I prefer Netgear routers over Linksys routers is that Netgear has no limit (or a very high limit) on the number of devices that you can list by MAC number and tell the router to "allow only these devices to connect to the network". I use this feature as an extra firewall, and find that the Linksys 25-device list is inadequate for my needs.

Finally, the Netgear "Genie" app for managing the router settings is clear and easy to understand. The initial setup for this router is easy, unless you have a nonstandard home network (e.g., my router is connected with the Comcast-supplied equipment in "Bridge" mode), and/or you interrupt the setup routine before it's run through all its steps. If you do land in setup limbo, you can start over by resetting the router to the factory settings (use a paperclip to hold down the reset button for 10-30 seconds--light will blink; unplug from wall for 30 seconds; follow Quick Start instructions again from beginning).
text_fidelity_b: Netgear R7500-200NAS Nighthawk X4 Ultimate Gaming Router - AC2350 4X4 MU-MIMO Dual Band WiFi Gigabit Router (R7500v2) with Open Source Support. Compatible with Amazon Echo/Alexa

text_fidelity_a: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White We have all three of the Echo products: The Dot, The Tap, and the original Echo. The Dot works very similarly to the original Echo. You say the wake word, you give a command or question, it responds. It does have a speaker itself, but it doesn't get as loud as the original Echo or the Tap. All of the devices will sync together in one Amazon app, but they all still work independently. Meaning, if I set an alarm on the Dot, only the alarm on the Dot goes off. But with the app on my phone, I can access all the devices in the one place. The Original Echo is better for larger areas. the Dot is ideal if you already have a sound system you would like to connect the Dot to, or small spaces like bathrooms or bedrooms. The Dot is great for kids. My daughter has it in her room so she can ask it how to spell words and such. The Tap is an entirely different beast, in my opinion. No wake word. Touch and talk. But it works via Bluetooth and wifi for on the go use using your cellular device. The Echo Dot does not come with a remote. Like the Original Echo, it needs to be plugged into the wall and needs wifi. (The Tap has a chargeable battery.) They are all great devices, though Amazon still has some work to be done on them. Each has a different place where it is the ideal choice, so which you should choose really depends on your needs.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

text_fidelity_a:
Cisco-Linksys E4200 Dual-Band Wireless-N Router,Black I bought the Cisco E4200 and the Asus RT-N56U. The RT-N56U was better than the E4200 in strength and speed. Transferring files from laptop to NAS server was much faster with the ASUS both wired and wireless. I however decided to stay with the Cisco because the attached USB hard drive (NTFS) works flawlessly with Windows Backup (not the case with the RT-N56U).

Anyhow, I just switched to AT&T U-verse and tried to have the E4200 get an internet IP address automatically. For some reason it didn't. The ASUS here performed great, as soon as I plugged the cable from AT&T modem/router it configured itself. Amazing! Again... I need those backups in NTFS drives, otherwise I would stick with the RT-N56U.

After trying to troubleshoot myself and losing connection with their chat support, I had to call tech support (in India or surrounding areas). I spent almost hour and a half on the phone, resetting and rebooting everything. The router would just not get an internet IP address. They suggested that the router may be defective, but that I should call AT&T and see if there was something they could do on their end???

Instead of doing that, I drove to my sister house and got her E4200(I did the same setup in her house the week before and it worked well). When I plugged it in, it got the internet IP address immediately, no problems at all.

Both routers had the exact same firmware and settings which indicated to me that the problem was most likely with my E4200.

Again to call Cisco tech support. I explained what happened and told the tech that I had disconnected the router, and that I wanted a replacement. After many questions about how many PCs and laptops I had in my house -irrelevant to the case-, he asked me if there was a cable in lan port one, I replied NO, then he asked the same question about port 2, I replied NO, and so on, until he asked me if there was power going to the router, to which I obviously reply NO. So he said sarcastically 'how do you expect the router to work if it is disconnected?'. I replied 'what part of "I disconnected the router" you did not understand. Misunderstandings like this happened with all the technicians I spoke to.

Another one told me that I had voided my warranty for upgrading the firmware in the router. She scolded me for doing so stating that 3rd party firmware can have bricked the router. I explained to her that I downloaded the firmware from the Cisco support website. She kept going on. I am still trying to figure out where she got the idea that I got 3rd party firmware. What a show of ignorance!

When I asked for a supervisor, they put me on hold for 28 min. After that I was told that there was nobody available. Then the call got mysteriously disconnected when I asked the tech for his full name and badge number.

It is not only Cisco, I know. Many companies do it this way. But it is upsetting that Cisco can not source people who understand and speak English well enough to have a professional conversation. Based on this experience I wonder if these Cisco 'technicians' hold at least a high school diploma.
Yeah, they offer support 24-7-365, but it is not real support if they can not help you or even understand you.

My final advice, if you go for it, test the every single feature of the router. If you find any flaw, deal with Amazon, exchange it or get a refund. Do not try to deal with Cisco-Linksys. It is not worth the aggravation.
text_fidelity_b: Cisco-Linksys E4200 Dual-Band Wireless-N Router,Black

text_fidelity_a:
ViewSonic VA2359-SMH 23 Inch IPS 1080p LED Monitor with HDMI and VGA Inputs What I like about this monitor:
1. Easy to set up - I used my previous monitor video cable and power cord and had it up and running in a few minutes.
2. Very clear resolution despite having an old video card.
3. It has an HDMI connection but I am using the regular VGA input and it still very clear.
4. A VGA and sound cord are included.
5. Very sleek, streamline black design which goes nicely with my other computer accessories.

What could be better:
1. The included instructions tell you nothing about how to make video and audio adjustments. I can't use a bright setting and it took a good while to figure out how to use the buttons underneath the screen. They are not intuitive at all.
2. Poor Audio - if you want good audio from this monitor that will not be possible. It is a thin monitor and the audio is very thin and tinny. I was hoping I could disconnect my external sound system to make more room on my desk but found out that I must keep it if I want to hear any decent sound from my computer.
3. While testing the volume on this monitor you must still figure out how to toggle using the various buttons underneath. There is no single volume button or toggle switch. And it will not get very loud.
4. If you don't bump the monitor or use the toggle switches the monitor stays fairly steady on it's stand. Otherwise it will rock and jiggle while using the buttons.
5. No HDMI cable is included.

The scant instructions did say to visit their website to download the latest drivers but as of yet this monitor is not listed in their driver drop down window. I don't think that matter much at this time as the monitor is very clear and sharp.
Overall: Good monitor for the price (as of this review it costs $138.24 Prime) which I feel is a fair price.
text_fidelity_b: ViewSonic VA2359-SMH 23 Inch IPS 1080p LED Monitor with HDMI and VGA Inputs

Echo Show 5 (1st Gen, 2019 release) -- Smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Sandstone I purchased a pair of these in September 2020 - one for me, and one for my wife - and am surprised by how much I have become dependent upon it. It reads from my google calendar two hours from a scheduled event, so that is one useful feature. If I cannot remember a fact or quickly need to look up something, all I have to do is ask. I also use it as a clock.

Except for the visual display of time and date, I could have accomplished everything I mentioned with my old hockey puck, A.K.A. "Dot." However, for some reason I did not use that one as much, so, perhaps the visual display catches my eye and reminds me that I have a fairly useful appliance that will do things for me. At any rate I use this a LOT more than I did the Dot.

The real user in the house if my wife. She is constantly interacting with her Echo, but she was the household power user when she was using a Dot as well. While I feel as though I have gotten my money's worth from mine, the truth is my wife's daily (hourly?) use of hers makes the pair we have in our own home work spaces a bargain.

Bottom line: cool device that has numerous uses - many of which I don't personally use. For some reason the screen inspires me to use mine a lot more than the screenless Dot, and honestly I rarely use the Echo visually.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Show 5 (1st Gen, 2019 release) -- Smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Sandstone

Also, the Kindle Fire tends to get really heavy after you have held it for a while. It seems they could have found a way to make it as attractive and still lighter.
