text_fidelity_a:
Munitio SV Mobile Performance Earphones with 3 Button Mic Control, Bronze Lower and mid end earphones have generally been lacking in both quality and performance. Given my propensity to misplace them, I have been reluctant to invest in more expensive versions. But with increased reliance on mobile devices, it was most definitely time to upgrade.

My familiarity with Munitio was more from their urban chic style complete with bullet motif, Kevlar coated cord, "tactical" carrying case and "hollow point" ear cups. At the risk of looking more Duck dynasty than cool, I was eager to try them.

Designed for use with Apple devices, the phones come securely packaged in a black carrying case. The look is sleek and modern and the bronze color is appealing. These are also available in black and gray. There are three sets of ear cups in different sizes. They were comfortable and shut out outside noise. The cord is flat and tangle free with a heft that promises durability. The 3 button mic control is located on the upper left hand side of the earphone cable. I really couldn't see the buttons but quickly mastered them by touch. They provide full functionality for calls and music on iPods, iPods and iPhones and just music for other mp3 players and Android devices.

I encountered no difficulties in making or taking calls. I could hear the other party and they could hear me without difficulty. The mic is positioned close enough to the mouth and is sufficiently sensitive that I didn't have to scream or repeat things. I made calls from a fairly busy coffee shop and a mall and ambient noise did not impair the call quality.

I tried these earphones with my IPod and a cheap mp3 player of dubious lineage. The sound was clear, strong and enjoyable. I did not find the bass overwhelming and was generally pleased with the performance.

Bottom line, I liked these earphones. The case and the trio of ear cups are thoughtful touches. Although light, there is a sense of substance and quality. The controls are intuitive and easy to use. There is a two year limited warranty. Serving up generous doses of comfort, convenience and performance, these ear phones are right on target.
text_fidelity_b: Munitio SV Mobile Performance Earphones with 3 Button Mic Control, Bronze

PROS: These are super light weight stands that will prop up pretty much any phone or tablet. They are adequate for their purpose. The stand can be adjusted to any position, and the spot that the device rests on is generous. Small, light and easy to carry around these have convenience in portability. Also, as I have the multi pack, you can place them all over or share. Or lose some, haha. Best value is multi pack. Single price is too much for quality of this product.

CONS: They claim anti-skid, but it fails in that feature. So lightweight that if you intend to tap at your device often, depending on what surface you have this placed on, it will scoot around some. I recommend modifying it with a couple beads (or line) of hot glue to give it a rubbery bottom. Or use a scrap of rug pad (that non slip material), or simply use it on a less smooth/hard surface. If just needing to prop up phone or tablet, then it will stay put. The kickstand is solid.

I am most comfortable using it on a smaller device if only because these have barely any weight to them. I have a much heavier stand that I prefer to use, but the price for one is significant. These are basic, light weight and super budget friendly (for multi pack).

Would make for a good stocking stuffer!

In my pics, I am demonstrating this product with pixel phone and LGtablet

text_fidelity_a:
PIONEER Truly Wireless in-Ear Headphones, Black, SE-C8TW(B) If you're an iphone user, you're probably wondering whether to buy these Pioneer wireless headphones or the Apple version. The Pioneer price is about 1/3 cheaper than Apple. The Pioneer earbuds fit in your ear, so you get much better sound and much better sound isolation. These are nowhere near as detailed or loud as similarly priced wired headphones, but that's true of all wireless Bluetooth earbuds. I will say the connection is stable and not noisy, so these are better than most cheap Bluetooth earbuds. There is some bass, but don't work well for bass-heavy music. Maximum volume is just OK. Battery life is only about 3 hours per charge (compared to 5 hours for Apple), then you have to put the earbuds back in the case for a 1 hour charge. 3 hours may be enough for you; you have to decide, but 5 hours is certainly going to be more interesting to most people. The charging case is much larger than the Apple charging case. The case is 3.3 inches long and 2.2 inches wide. These case is to big to fit comfortably in my pants pocket, so I would only carry it with me in a backpack or purse.

Usage is pretty simple. They paired easily with my phone as a normal Bluetooth device. The buttons on the headphones are easy to use. They are comfortable in my ears. They are secure enough so far, never feeling like they are going to fall out. They are not noticeably heavy like some earbuds can be. When in my ears, they are much less ugly than the Apple earbuds.

I would give these 5 stars for the price and performance if the sound and battery life were better. Frankly, I've tried a few different totally wireless earbuds and been less than impressed by all of them. Bluetooth headphones that have a wire connecting the two pieces can be had for much lower prices and have much better sound quality and much better battery life. Removing the wire just doesn't seem worth the downsides to me.
text_fidelity_b: PIONEER Truly Wireless in-Ear Headphones, Black, SE-C8TW(B)

text_fidelity_a:
Bang & Olufsen Beoplay E8 2.0 True Wireless Earphones - Pink, One Size - 1646112 These earbuds are pricey, but they are easily the best sounding earbuds that I have ever tried. I listen to mostly acoustic music where detail is more important than boomy bass. The bass on these earbuds is great for me without being boomy. The higher frequency detail is incredible. I can hear things with these that just don't come through with other brands of earbuds. The quiet sections of a song are very quiet through these earbuds, so the soft sections are even clearer. Stereo separation is excellent so I feel like I'm right there in the room with the musicians.

Volume is excellent. With other brands of wireless earbuds, I usually have to turn the volume all the way up and even then the music is often too quiet. WIth these B&O earbuds, I never have the volume at more than 2/3 power.

4 hour battery life is average for premium true-wireless earbuds and somewhat better than the cheaper models. The charging case is compact enough to fit in my pocket (unlike some other brands) and works flawlessly. I love that is uses USB-C, just like my smartphone. It also supports wireless charging, which I don't use with my phone either. USB-C is easier for me to understand.

As with all earbuds, picking the right ear tips is an important part of getting the best sound. I love that they included memory foam ear tips in the box. The memory foam tips are the most comfortable and best sounding tips for me. I can listen to these for hours without any discomfort.

There is an official B&O Android app that connects to the earbuds that has a few interesting features. It shows the earbud battery life, which is nice to have, especially if I don't remember when was the last time I charged them. There are some listening modes, that are somewhat customizable (but not like a traditional equalizer, which would be easier for me to understand). There is also a transparency feature that lets me hear background sound through the earbuds (useful when walking on the street or listening for an airport announcement). The earbuds do work fine without the app if you pair them with your phone using the normal Bluetooth setup.

These earbuds are not designed for sports. When I'm running or working out, I use my Jaybird earbuds that are more secure in my ears and are waterproof. The B&O earbuds are more comfortable and better sounding than my Jaybirds, so I use them more often.
text_fidelity_b: Bang & Olufsen Beoplay E8 2.0 True Wireless Earphones - Pink, One Size - 1646112

text_fidelity_a:
Marware Revolve Portrait and Landscape Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Black (will not fit HDX models) Overall, this is a fine case for the 8.9 inch Fire HD. The overall quality is quite nice - I have other Marware products for my Kindle Touch, and it's good to see that they are continuing to maintain a strong focus on product quality. All the materials feel nice; the stitching is tight and even; there's ample cushioning for tablet protection while maintaining a slim profile; and the elastic strap holds the cover closed in a secure fashion.

I also like how Marware packages their products with a minimum of packaging waste but still ensures the product can travel through the mail without being dinged up. The package is also easy to open - no fuss, no muss.

I initially had some difficulty getting the Fire into the case. The Fire is held in place using a plastic cradle, but it seemed to be too small. I had to (gasp!) resort to reading the user guide that came with it, and found out I needed to position it in a certain way and then snap it in. When it is properly inserted you'll hear and feel a clear "snap" at each of the four corners of the tablet. When properly installed the case holds the tablet very securely. I shook it vigorously (over a thick cushion in case it failed) and the Fire stayed put.

My main quibble is with the rotation feature. I was really looking forward to this since some apps only run in portrait mode; others only in landscape. While the rotation feature works, it is very stiff - you really have to twist hard to get it to rotate. It's a two-handed operation: one hand to rotate the tablet; the other to hold the case while you're turning.

The bottom of the cradle has a tab that fits into a slot on the base of the cover to prop up the tablet. This works in both landscape and portrait modes. There are three tabs so you can adjust the angle.

There are cut outs for the power and HDMI ports. I had no problems accessing any of the ports, power button or volume controls while it was in the cover.

Since I often end up having to charge the Fire while it is in use, I rotated the screen so the power plug is at the top. That allows me to keep the tablet propped up on my desk in landscape mode for video watching, but still use the power cord.

It also offers an auto on/off ability - the Fire turns off when you close the cover, and wakes up when you open the cover. It's a nice feature and it works well.

It has a slot on the cover so you can fit your hand into it for ease of holding it. That has value, but what I would have preferred to have instead (or in addition to) is a pocket on either the inside or the outside to hold items such as a cleaning cloth. This is not a huge problem, but I'll certainly miss that since the case for my original Fire has a outside pouch that is great for holding a cleaning cloth and a small stylus.

I'm going to give this 5 stars, but 4.5 is more accurate given the reluctance of the rotation feature. But, since it does everything else very well, looks good, and feels nice, it's closer to a 5 rating than a 4.
text_fidelity_b: Marware Revolve Portrait and Landscape Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Black (will not fit HDX models)

text_fidelity_a:
ANNKE C800 4K 8MP PoE Security Camera with Audio Recording, 4K Ultra HD IP Turret Camera, 100ft EXIR 2.0 Night Vision, H.265+, IP67 Weatherproof, Support 256GB SD Card(Not Included) When I initially saw this camera it checked most of the boxes I look for when looking for security cameras. It is PoE, has H.265, ONVIF support allowing use with Blue Iris, Sony IMX274 Starvis Sensor. Once I received this camera and began digging into it I quickly realized certain important facts.

Most importantly, this is a rebranded Hikvision camera. This is among the companies that has been discovered spying on the US using their cameras - the firmware this camera comes with is long outdated and, in fact, can not be updated to anywhere close to what is current. This is far too risky for me to install on my system.

Any camera you install on your system should have the latest firmware installed and you need to have a good understanding of network security protocols. Cameras such as this one, that are older versions of cameras made by manufacturers that are blacklisted - while still being sold, people who understand the industry avoid them - are an invitation for hackers to invade your system.

While the specs on and price of this camera seem decent - this is not a camera I recommend. This poses far more risks than it is worth.
text_fidelity_b: ANNKE C800 4K 8MP PoE Security Camera with Audio Recording, 4K Ultra HD IP Turret Camera, 100ft EXIR 2.0 Night Vision, H.265+, IP67 Weatherproof, Support 256GB SD Card(Not Included)

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Basics HDMI to RCA Converter We have a minivan with a DVD entertainment system pre-installed. It predates the HDMI standard, so there are just RCA analog inputs in the back of the van. Since DVDs are pretty much obsolete, using this adapter we are able to plug in a laptop, raspberry pi or other digital video player to the car's system. I like that it is powered by USB, it is a convenient source of power especially when you don't have access to outlets (like in a car!). But you have to be careful about ground loop feedback. When powering it off a laptop, and the laptop is charging in the car, it can create either an audible hum and/or visual static distortion pattern on the video feed. This is common in DC circuits that share ground when working with analog equipment, unfortunately. I'm not sure if there's much that can be done about it other than try to run off batteries as often as possible (with this converter attached to a USB battery bank, the laptop on its own power, and the car running its own 12v DC). I have an older similar product looks almost identical that does the same thing so I'm guessing that's just a side effect of working with RCA inputs instead of digital ones.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics HDMI to RCA Converter

text_fidelity_a:
TomTom GO 2535TM World Traveler 5-Inch Bluetooth GPS Navigator with Lifetime Traffic & Maps and Voice Recognition (Discontinued by Manufacturer) The TOMTOM GO2535 TM WTE is quite attractive with a large screen and smooth appearance but because of its size, this is a heavier GPS than many others. A magnetic plug attaches the power supplies either to a computer with its USB plug or to a car with its accessory power plug. As with most GPS devices, no "home" DC power supply is included. I have found the car mount to be great, easy to attach and remove from the windshield with a simple turn. My only complaint with the mount is that it takes some work to direct the device to a visible position and I fear that it will not last as long as the GPS. The magnetic plug slips into a cutout in the mount, allowing it to remain in position so the GPS can quickly be inserted or removed for safekeeping.
As for the functionality of the GPS, it has some problems, thereby preventing me from giving this a 5 star review. I'll simply list the Pros and Cons.
Pros:
Start up time is quick and option to start from last destination can save time if the satellite connection is delayed.
Menu options are easily learned even if at first they seem to include extra steps.
Responds quickly to need for alternate route when a turn is missed.
Ease in moving through functions on screen.
POIs are expansive and easy to discover
Map identifies a location I frequent which is not identified by any other GPS I've used.
Identifies traffic light cameras adequately. Have yet to receive speed camera warning.
Voice commands are intuitive and a little printed card is included if you're in need of prompting.
Connectivity to my Mac is easy and the option to automatically check for updates can save time.

Cons:
Speed is not always accurate. Often has my car going at 10 mph less than actual speed.
When setting a new destination, I've been unable to change the state unless I do it using the voice command. This may be possible, but I haven't had the time to investigate. Since I'm in a metropolitan area and may venture through 2 states and the District of Columbia in less than an hour, it's important for me to access the individual states.
When using phone through the GPS, although I can hear the conversation with no problem, the person on the other end of my call can't hear me clearly. Every time I've used it with a phone, the call has been dropped. I've never had a call dropped otherwise with my phone or other Bluetooth capable device.
Does not recognize voice commands at times.
Voice prompts are very frequent and I'd love to be able to reduce them but not turn it off.
Seldom comes up with the routes I usually take, even with a second try after selecting the Change Route option.

All in all, this is a good GPS navigation device and the lifetime updates are a definite advantage. I haven't traveled the wold with it, but will update my review as necessary with observations internationally. I do know the maps are on the device because I saw them when I performed the update last week and couldn't figure out how to get back to the USA on the device. For some reason, TOMTOM put me in the UK even though I'm registered in the USA and confirmed that selection.

What's interesting is that I still prefer my 3-year-old Navigon for its ease of use, accuracy and lovely displays, with two exceptions. I do not care for their customer service or necessity to download map updates to the device's SD card instead of doing a direct update on a Mac. This TOMTOM excels there and it comes in a very definite second for any GPS I've used. When the time comes for my beloved Navigon to bite the dust, I feel confident that I'll still be happy with this TOMTOM.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom GO 2535TM World Traveler 5-Inch Bluetooth GPS Navigator with Lifetime Traffic & Maps and Voice Recognition (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Belkin

I got the Belkin Bluetooth Receiver [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492-P Bluetooth Music Receiver]] but I had complaints about range. Even though there is a fix (which requires opening it up and removing a metal piece which other reviewers have said is just added to add some weight)the range with the fix still is not up to par. The Sound quality was below par as well.

__________________
Apple Airport Express

The Apple Airport Express is unique in solving my problem as it has one major advantage... It uses the wireless network in my home to stream music to my receiver (not Bluetooth). Awesome idea and I actually ordered one. This way I could be way out of Bluetooth range (i.e. my backyard)and still control music through my iPhone or iPad through the wireless network.
The only problem with this setup (which in the end I refused to deal with) is that you can only use your iPhone or iPad as a REMOTE to control iTunes on a computer. Meaning that you need to have a computer on with the appropriate songs on at all times if you want to listen to music. Being that we have laptops only and there is no consistent computer in the house, let alone "on", and connected to the wireless network.
This could not work for me.
Second problem with this system is that you can only play iTunes. No Pandora or other music venues such as youtube etc.
And to top it all off this Apple Airport express cost $99!!(plus the use of a computer full time)

_______________________
Logitech Wireless Speaker Adapter for Bluetooth Audio Devices

This is very similar to the Belkin but it literally took 2 minutes to hook up and the range that I tested so far is incredible. That being said it is using Bluetooth not Wireless Network so don't expect total wireless connectivity. The Sound quality is on par with the apple but I assume that will degrade with distance to the receiver. Other wise it is perfect.

In summation I am very happy with this product at this price. I would gladly pay $100-$200 for a system like the Apple Airport express that could play all audio from my iPhone or iPad directly and didn't require me to only use my iPhone as a remote for a computer that can only play iTunes on the network.... Until a reasonable system comes out like that I think this product will do the job nicely.

Or if your so inclined you can quickly rack up a few thousand dollars setting up a Sonos System[[ASIN:B005441AJC Sonos Play:3 All-In-One Wireless Music Player With 3 Integrated Speakers (Black, NEW)]]
But My house is already wired with speakers and such and I don't feel it is worth the investment.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Wireless Speaker Adapter for Bluetooth Audio Devices
